The bigger story was the formally signed US-Iran MOU (June 17), which reopened the Strait of Hormuz and crashed Brent crude ~11%, falling further to ~$73/barrel by July — down ~40% from the April war peak. Goldman Sachs confirmed its 12-month US recession probability at 15% on June 22. US data since has been mixed: May PCE hit a three-year-high 4.1%, June jobs slowed sharply to +57,000, and June CPI cooled to 3.5%. China's Q2 GDP slowed to 4.3% (slowest in 3.5 years) and the IMF's July WEO flagged stalled disinflation, while the Section 122 tariff cliff is now just 8 days away with Section 301 fallback tariffs facing a timing gap.
